meta.subtitle: Multi-tenant Supabase / Next.js booking app
meta.headline: One cross-tenant read was proven live and one N+1 will not survive traffic. The rest are hardening, test-quality, and maintainability wins — all with named fixes.
meta.scope: RLS policies, service-role code paths, API routes, auth/permission layer, the booking and billing modules, and the test suite.
meta.methodology: A live two-tenant stand-up (M2), Supabase RLS/advisor review (M1), vitals (hotspots), knip (dead code), jscpd (duplication), Stryker (mutation testing on money-critical code), and the M9 static Server Action/boundary detectors. Every finding passes a correctness check (repro/evidence) and an applicability check.

findings.title: Cross-tenant read proven: user A can read user B's bookings
findings.evidence: On the stood-up stack, signed in as tenant A, a request to /rest/v1/bookings returned tenant B's rows. The policy uses USING (auth.role() = 'authenticated') — it checks that you're logged in, not that the row is yours.
findings.impact: Any signed-in customer can read every other customer's bookings, including names, dates, and contact details. This is a direct data-exposure incident, not a theoretical one.
findings.fix: Rewrite the policy to scope by owner: USING (user_id = auth.uid()). Re-run the cross-tenant matrix to confirm the boundary now holds.

findings.title: N+1 query on the dashboard loads one query per booking
findings.evidence: The dashboard fetches the booking list, then issues a separate customer lookup inside the render loop — N+1 queries that scale linearly with row count.
findings.impact: At 20 bookings the page is fine; at 2,000 it issues 2,000 queries per load and times out. This is what falls over on launch day.
findings.fix: Replace the per-row lookup with a single joined query (select with an embedded resource), or batch the customer IDs into one in() query.

findings.title: service_role key reachable from a client-imported module
findings.evidence: The admin client is instantiated with the service_role key in a module that is transitively imported by a client component. It is not currently called from the browser, but nothing prevents it.
findings.impact: The service_role key bypasses RLS entirely. A future accidental client import would bundle a master key to the database into the browser.
findings.fix: Move the admin client behind a server-only boundary and add import 'server-only' so an accidental client import fails the build.

findings.title: The refund guard has a test that can't fail
findings.evidence: Mutation testing: deleting the amount <= originalCharge check left every test green. No test asserts that an over-refund is rejected on money-critical logic.
findings.impact: A regression that allows refunding more than was charged would ship undetected — the suite would still pass.
findings.fix: Add one test asserting a refund greater than the original charge is rejected.

findings.title: PII sitting in three columns with no access policy
findings.evidence: Schema classification flagged three PII columns on a table whose RLS is enabled but whose SELECT grant is broader than the policy intends.
findings.impact: Personal contact data is more broadly readable than the app appears to intend — a privacy and compliance exposure.
findings.fix: Tighten the SELECT grant to match the intended policy, and confirm no client path reads these columns unnecessarily.

findings.title: A Server Action mutates without checking the caller
findings.evidence: The Server Action accepts a bookingId and cancels it with no ownership check — it trusts that the UI only offers the button on the user's own bookings.
findings.impact: Anyone who can call the action with an arbitrary bookingId can cancel another tenant's booking (IDOR via a Server Action).
findings.fix: Verify the booking belongs to auth.uid() inside the action before mutating; never rely on the UI to enforce authorization.

findings.title: Date-formatting logic copy-pasted across six components
findings.evidence: jscpd: the same timezone-handling block appears in six components, already diverged in two of them.
findings.impact: A fix to one copy silently misses the others — the two that diverged already render times differently.
findings.fix: Extract one formatBookingTime helper and replace the six copies.

findings.title: Hand-rolled session parsing where a library exists
findings.evidence: Custom cookie parsing and JWT decoding reimplement what the Supabase auth-helpers already provide, with an edge case that mishandles an expired token.
findings.impact: Fragile reinvented auth code — the exact category that quietly breaks and is hard to reason about.
findings.fix: Replace with the maintained Supabase auth-helpers session handling.

findings.title: app/api/webhook/route.ts is the #1 hotspot
findings.evidence: vitals: high complexity, 28 changes in 90 days, co-changes with 14 files.
findings.impact: Central, churny, and complex — a future-bug magnet with wide blast radius.
findings.fix: Decompose into handlers. High value but slow and risky — schedule as a planned refactor, not a quick win.

findings.title: No dead code worth pruning
findings.evidence: knip found 3 unused exports, all framework entry points — nothing to remove.
findings.impact: Clean. Noted for transparency; not every module produces a finding.
